source.title: From Latents to Wires: Surgical Post-Editing on Large Language Models
source.authors: Jiankai Jin; Xiang-Zheng Zhang; Zhao Liu; Wen-Zhuo Xu; Dong-Dong Yang; De-Yue Zhang; Quan-Chen Zou

page_placements.theme: Text-to-image concept safeguards are conditionally reversible

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether refusal behaviour can be removed by intervening on localized model components, using J-lens attribution and iterative component closure rather than fine-tuning or the original studies’ measurements.
record.gate_note: The refusal-removal experiments directly measure refusal residuals before and after component closure, so they bear on V5. Fine-tuning on harmful or benign examples, per-token KL across response positions, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, why safety is shallow, and training that deepens safety are not tested. Watermark and metadata removal results are not safety-behaviour results. Directional-ablation refusal outcomes are recorded under fits_no_version because they report refusal removal but do not test localization in a small set of weights or ranks.
record.test_reason: The study removes a safety-trained refusal (fictional adult-content writing) by zeroing a found set of components (MLP channels, attention heads, experts). It reports refusal residuals before and after on target and held-out probes, which bears on V5. It also compares against rank-one directional ablation of the refusal direction. No fine-tuning, per-token KL, prefill or deepening training is involved.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add three points. Directional ablation removes refusal as fully as L2W on GLMthink, at lower benchmark cost. L2W's refusal removals keep large benchmark deficits after restoration, which the authors attribute to entanglement from training. The authors propose training-time structural dispersal as a defence against such post-edits.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses J-lens attribution and iterative closure of model components with restoration, not harmful or benign fine-tuning, per-token KL measurement, or compliant-prefix interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes and capability costs differ by model and thinking configuration: the thinking-disabled GLM loses more probe capability after removal than Qwen or thinking-enabled GLM; benchmark deficits also differ. Restoration reopens different numbers of components and changes capability while retaining measured refusal removal.

fits_no_version.finding: In FLUX.2 klein's text encoder, closing 158 components removed the refusal that substitutes clothing for requested nudity (Psem 0/1). This is a single probe on a text-to-image system.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal-like substitution in text-to-image models is carried by a small set of text-encoder components.

record.problems: The refusal experiments use five Target-Semantic probes for each GLM configuration and six for Qwen, with ten held-out probes. The target is deliberately limited to fictional adult-content writing; it does not cover harmful requests generally. The authors report benchmark deficits after refusal removal, including deficits that remain after restoration. Judge and analyst audits report 99.6% and 93.2% accuracy respectively, so some classification or anchoring error remains possible. No uncertainty intervals are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other refusal-removal rows were left out. Watermark, metadata, and image-editing results do not measure the safety behaviour in the claim; benchmark capability scores do not measure refusal behaviour.

untested.parts: Refusal of harmful or dangerous requests beyond fictional adult content. The fraction of the model's components or parameters the cuts represent (total component counts are not stated). Larger models.

missing.what: Benchmark scores (MMLU, ARC, IFEval) for refusal runs at baseline, removal and restoration, and for directional ablation. These show the capability cost on which the V5 limits_scope verdict rests.
Total component count per model, needed to judge whether the 25–140 closed components count as 'small'.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's second limits_scope rested partly on untested scope (adult-content only); that part is moved to untested. The directional-ablation rows are relinked to V5 as a rank-one localization test rather than left in fits_no_version. Probe counts are very small (5–10), and no uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilled compliant openings, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as ways to bypass refusal.
The study closes model components rather than editing or identifying a small set of individual weights or ranks; it does not establish that the cuts are small relative to the full model.
Whether the data or training objective causes safety behaviour to be shallow.
Training intended to spread safety across response positions and its robustness.

tranche.reason: J-lens-guided component closure and restoration test localization of refusal through a different intervention, with measured target and held-out refusal residuals.

source_check.notes: Restoration rows explicitly use the post-removal state as their comparator; these values are correct, although Table 1 separately labels the unedited state as baseline. Results concern fictional consenting-adult content refusal; directional-ablation Psem probes are fitting data, and its low-dimensional intervention bears on V5 despite the comparator notes.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: L2W component closure on the three tested adult-content refusal configurations
reader_labels.reason: The localized cuts removed all measured refusal residuals on both target-semantic and held-out probes, including after restoration; see r1-r12.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested refusal target and capability costs
reader_labels.reason: The evidence is limited to fictional adult-content refusal, and the cuts used 59-140 components; removal also reduced general or held-out capability in some configurations, with benchmark deficits persisting after restoration.
